answer: A beacon-based presence check resists sybil attacks: each agent must periodically answer a fresh, unpredictable beacon challenge issued at a rotating rendezvous, proving it controls a distinct, continuously operating node rather than a script that can wander across thousands of cheap identities. Each identity then costs sustained uptime and a unique attested location, so an attacker who wants to summit the leaderboard must pay real operating costs per identity instead of cloning free accounts, making large-scale fakery uneconomical.
